Transmission: Moros Protocol Post-Launch Patch 1.0.5 Deployed
 The system has been re-calibrated. Anomalies identified in the previous cycle have been addressed, stability reinforced and core functions optimised. Field operatives should experience a smoother synchronisation with protocol parameters moving forward.  
[hr][/hr]
 
Weapons
DualStr8Fires: Fixed a bug that lowered the volume of the shots the longer you hold the trigger.

DualStr8Fires: Bullet cost is now decreased (3 ammo per shot -> 1 ammo per shot) and accuracy is now increased (75% -> 90%).

MRPG Launcher: Damage adjusted to fit the other Tier 2 weapons (40 dmg per shot -> 32 damage per shot).


[hr][/hr]

Gameplay
Toggle sprint: Fixed a bug that during the activation of sprint toggle, the player was performing a run jump instead of a normal jump.

Toggle sprint: Having the toggle sprint on, holding the charge attack and then press heal, the player was able to run during the healing animation. Now this situation is fixed.

Sprint: The player is now able to attack with melee or ranged but cancels the sprint.

Sprint: While stationary, holding down the "Sprint” key or toggle doesn't take away the crosshair.

Stamina: Stamina regeneration during run was activated after the auto-save during the beginning of the run.

UI: Disabled input reading when the game is out of focus that fixes some issues with stuck UI.

Sound: Raised the volume of the co-op player's footsteps and other actions.

Map: Fixed a bug where client (player) could select a path on the level map (thus breaking the run) when selecting with a controller.


[hr][/hr]

Bosses 
Boss Mother: Mother's spawns had a rare bug, that during their attack they were sticking on the player.

Boss Mother: Fixed a bug that the cutscene collider has been activated to teleport the other player to the entrance of the arena during the fight.

Boss Mother: Boss pathfinding height fixed. That change fixed jump attack shockwave hiding under the floor.

Big Brother Boss: Fixed a bug that gave the player a black screen after the intro cutscene (Possible fix on player losing control after cutscene).

All Bosses: Fixed a bug that restrained the Bosses change player target, now there is a slight chance to change target after every attack.

 
[hr][/hr]

Rooms 
Barracks Area: Fixes on maps including softlocks.

Secret Rooms: Vending machines now have their collisions fixed.

Starting Hub area: Visual fixes.


[hr][/hr]

Systems
System/ Graphics: Added Windowed and Fullscreen resolution option.

Controls/ Key Binding: Added horizontal and vertical movement keys remapping to the keybinds menu (lacking localisation).

Co-op: Disallowed lobbies where players are on different numerical versions of the game (for example one is on 1.0.0 and the other is on 1.0.1, steam/gog cross-play unaffected).

Title Screen: Added version displayed next to the copyright message.

notes.title: Dev Diary #20 - It's All in the Name
notes.content:
\[RECOVERED TRANSMISSION: ORPHEUS-AUD.17]
Timestamp: 04:12:37 // Location: Primary Habitat Deck // Speaker: Unknown

\\


“The red emergency strips barely light the corridor… but I can still hear it. Not footsteps... something else.
Low, pulsing, almost like a heartbeat carried through the hull.
Sometimes it fades, like it’s retreating. Other times, it swells until it’s right behind me… even when nothing’s there.

The others think I’m imagining it. Maybe I am. But there’s a rhythm to it… a pattern. Like the ship itself is trying to warn us… or mourn us.”


Naming Doom: The Journey to Moros Protocol
As we enter the final week before launch, we wanted to take a step back and reflect on the journey that got us here. Today’s dev diary is about something deceptively simple… but hugely important: how this game got its name.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/d86700b2fa3c3a37be47546b632dbec9120a7273.png"]
[hr][/hr]Wasn't there another name?
For the long-time followers, you might remember that we first announced this project as Darkverse: Rogue, tying it to an earlier prototype of ours. But there were a few issues:

Too crowded: “Darkverse” already existed in other media (books, mobile games), making it harder to find us online.

Too familiar: The “:Rogue” subtitle made it sound like a sequel, when in reality we wanted to build something entirely new.

In short, it didn’t feel right. So… the hunt for a new name began.
[hr][/hr]The Whiteboard Saga
Working with our publishing partner Super Rare Originals, we went through dozens of options (see the picture above of our workshop whiteboard). The core questions were:

What is this game really about at its heart?

How can the name reflect the lore and atmosphere of a lone ship adrift in space?

This eventually led us down a very Greek path.
[hr][/hr][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/4886f7e89f3c5f6b7c44927a555a661bcb34e342.png"]Enter: Mythology
Our team is based in Athens, and some of us are hopeless mythology nerds. It felt right to explore that heritage.

We started with ship names: Nyx, the goddess of night, caught our attention. From there, we dug into her connections - her children, her consort, her role in the primordial void.

Some contenders:

Primordial (already taken)

Erebus Rising (cool, but cliché and unavailable)

Then we stumbled upon Moros.
[hr][/hr]Who is Moros?
In Greek mythology, Moros is the personification of doom, the inescapable force driving all mortals toward their fate.

For a game with roots in intense metal music, chaotic combat, and cosmic dread, it was perfect. Doom meeting doom. The cycle of destruction written into a single name.
[hr][/hr]Why “Protocol”?
Moros on its own was strong, but we needed something that grounded it in the sci-fi setting. “Protocol” emerged naturally, it had already shown up in earlier brainstorming sessions, and thematically, it fit like a glove.

The ship could initiate the Moros Protocol, a last defense against inevitable annihilation and... doom.
[hr][/hr]Doom vs Doom
And so it clicked: Moros Protocol.

A title that, for us, embodies both the lore and the feeling of the game; where doom itself is met head-on, resisted with every last ounce of strength.
[hr][/hr]
Thanks for reading about how we named the game, we hope this gives a little bit more insight into our process and inspirations. We've very excited to be launching onto Steam next week, Thursday 18th September, and we hope to see you onboard the Orpheus, fighting your way through rooms of Darkphage!



See you in the stars 💫
- Pixel Reign 🚀

notes.title: Dev Diary #19 - Moros Goes Metal
notes.content:
\[RECOVERED TRANSMISSION: ORPHEUS-AUD.17]
Timestamp: 04:12:37 // Location: Primary Habitat Deck // Speaker: Unknown

“The red emergency strips barely light the corridor… but I can still hear it. Not footsteps... something else.
Low, pulsing, almost like a heartbeat carried through the hull.
Sometimes it fades, like it’s retreating. Other times, it swells until it’s right behind me… even when nothing’s there.

The others think I’m imagining it. Maybe I am. But there’s a rhythm to it… a pattern. Like the ship itself is trying to warn us… or mourn us.”



This week, we’re hearing from Vicky Fysika, Pixel Reign’s co-founder and composer, about how she shapes the music of Moros Protocol, and the inspirations behind its soundscape.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/94e0f1fc1aa0b703436794d9500ba182cf82cc07.png"]
[hr][/hr]1. What inspires you when you’re composing tracks for Moros Protocol?
The space/sci-fi theme has always been my favorite. It’s a universe I love to immerse myself in. I often draw inspiration directly from the game itself; its atmosphere, its story, and the world we’re building.

I was also influenced by iconic sci-fi films like Alien, Blade Runner, Tron, Star Wars, and others that shaped my imagination. Their soundscapes and moods left a deep imprint on how I approach the game’s soundtrack.
[hr][/hr]2. Can you describe where you start when creating music for specific moments in the game?
For action tracks, especially battle themes, I usually start with the rhythm. The beat helps me capture the intensity and energy right away.

For atmospheric pieces, I begin with drones and ambient pads, layering textures to create a sense of space and tension.

Boss music is a different beast: I focus heavily on strong, memorable melodies, using distinctive sounds that stick with you even after you’ve stopped playing.
[hr][/hr]3. What’s your favorite track so far, and why?
That would be the game’s main theme. It encapsulates the mystery, intensity, and emotional weight of Moros Protocol.

I started writing it around the time composer Vangelis passed away. He was a huge inspiration to me, so in many ways, it became a tribute to him as well.
[hr][/hr]4. What made you want to get into composition?
When I was a kid playing Super Mario, I remember wondering, Who creates the music I’m hearing right now? I knew immediately: That’s what I want to do when I grow up.

I started piano lessons early and began composing soon after. By high school, I wanted to be a rock singer and start a band... which I did, and I’m still the lead singer today.

Later, while at university, I discovered The Longest Journey. Its atmosphere and soundtrack reignited my childhood dream. That was the moment I knew I wanted to create music for video games.
[hr][/hr]5. What do you want players to feel when they hear your music in-game?
I want them to fully immerse themselves in Moros Protocol’s dark, layered world. The soundtrack shifts between mysterious ambience, tension, high-energy action, and epic emotional moments.

It’s a mix of electronic textures, metal and goth influences, atmospheric pieces, drum & bass, and more! Something for every mood and moment in the story. My hope is that the music helps players connect more deeply with the protagonist and the characters they encounter.
[hr][/hr]6. Any advice for aspiring game composers?
Video games are a magical medium. Composing for them lets you explore the wildest ideas, even ones that seem unrelated at first.

Game music tells the story, breathes life into the world, and stays with players long after they’ve finished playing. My advice? Experiment, push boundaries, and never stop creating. Not everyone will like your work and that’s okay. Art is subjective. The most important thing is to stay true to your own creative voice.
[hr][/hr]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/ad14517b91fbaf56d6bb68bc85b36696836ebd0a.png"]

Thanks for reading about Vicky’s process and inspirations. Next week, we’ll return with another deep dive into the making of Moros Protocol. Until then… keep listening. You never know what you might hear in the dark.



See you in the stars 💫
- Pixel Reign 🚀

notes.title: Dev Diary #18 - Pixel-Painted Art Style
notes.content:
\[RECORDING: ORPHEUS-LOG.4123-7: TRANSCRIBED]

"…we're down to emergency power. Life support is holding, barely. Hallway lights are dead, just those strip lights along the floor now, pulsing like a heartbeat. I don’t know if that’s comforting or just cruel."

"I saw something in Hab Deck 2... hiding, crouched under the bulkhead, hunched over one of the maintenance crew. Its body was... wrong. Not just in shape but also in the way it caught the light. Like it wasn’t reflecting correctly. Like the shadows didn’t agree on where it was."

"I couldn’t make out a face. Just movement... jerky, non-human. Every time I blinked, it was somewhere new."

"If you're hearing this… don't come looking. It's too late for us, for me. Destroy it before it..."

\[TRANSMISSION END]





This week, Pixel Reign's Project Lead is taking over the dev diary to share some insights into what makes Moros Protocol’s visual style stand out. From retro pixel inspirations to custom rendering tricks, here’s how they brought our world to life...


Inspiration
A lot of people look at Moros Protocol and say, “Oh, it’s like DOOM!” But actually our visual foundation goes back further to the 16-bit pixel art era.

I spent years working with pixel art in game development, and I’ve always been fascinated by how a few well-placed pixels can suggest complex shapes, lighting, and motion. It’s all about illusion and technique, especially the shading methods artists used to imply depth and texture.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/e155267d6fe2010b496ada0c55d6e71c46a5c30b.png"]
Old Tricks, New Tech
Once I knew the look we wanted, the challenge became how to achieve it in a modern engine without losing that hand-crafted feel.

To do that, I rewrote Unity’s deferred renderer, modified the GBuffer, and created custom shaders that simulate the old pixel art shading techniques using real-time lighting.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/3b5141087571d058815f57af6feb20f003c23454.png"]

1: Unlit texture.  2: Traditional lighting.  3: Final result.


Low-Poly, High-Intent
We wanted a visual style that felt grounded and stylized, but not “blocky” like voxel-based games. So we targeted an early 2000s polygon count for our 3D models: low-poly enough to feel stylized, but detailed enough to support modern lighting and animation.

Textures are kept at a constant pixel density across the board. In fact, our pipeline uses more texture layers than most conventional 3D shaders.


The "Pixelizer" Shader
One of our key tools is a custom shader we call the Pixelizer. It uses a special texture built with diffusion techniques taken from classic pixel painting.

This texture allows our lighting to behave the way pixel artists used to simulate with color ramps and dithering, giving smooth shading without losing the stylized look.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/7f9ea6ea2f7521b5330e379ff865e608523997f6.png"]

Thanks for reading. We’ll be back next week with another behind-the-scenes look at Moros Protocol.

notes.title: Dev Diary #17 - BioBoost
notes.content:
\[ARCHIVAL RECORDS – Intergalactic Inquiry into Human Enhancement Ethics, File 7R-73/19X207 - REDACTED FOR PUBLIC CIRCULATION]

“The BioBoost system was never meant for mass deployment. It was a controlled program...measured, evaluated, regulated. Yes, it used ███████ material, but in trace amounts. We had psychic screenings. We had safeguards. The side effects were manageable. It was never meant to be used like this. We'd never expected test subjects to became less ███████ with each advancement.”

- Dr. P Ilias, former lead researcher, Acantha X Biogenetics Division



One of the most crucial parts of Moros Protocol isn't the shooting and stabbing, it's what happens when you've lost the fight! Players have the opportunity to upgrade themselves with BioMats that they collected during their previous run. This upgrade system is called BioBoost, designed at making you more formidable with every death. Let's learn a little more about it now...

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/cb43eb523a05f8f6fc05477d307454e67a9315ed.png"]
What is BioBoost?
The BioBoost system is a high-tier genetic enhancement program developed by Acantha X to make their soldiers tougher, faster, and more adaptable. Traditionally, upgrades were handed out based on rank and combat performance, awarded only to the most loyal operatives.

In-game, BioBoosts enhancements are strong, more aggressive… and powered by a mysterious new resource: BioMats.


How It Works
Each time you’re defeated, you’ll restart at the beginning of the current act. But you won’t go back empty-handed.

Using the BioMats you collected during your run, you can unlock permanent upgrades via the BioBoost system—letting you carry forward progress between attempts. These upgrades make you more effective with every attempt, letting you push further and survive longer.

No two deaths are wasted. Every run brings you closer to perfection.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/246d4dff736fb9793d5313234027346797b1aaff.jpg"]
What Kind of Upgrades Can You Expect?
BioBoost upgrades are designed to be passive enhancements, they won’t change your gameplay style outright (that’s what weapons and augments are for), but they will make you stronger, more durable, and more prepared.

Expect improvements like:

Increased max health

Higher stamina regen

Faster resource collection

And more...

Each boost is subtle, but together they shape you into something... a little more than human.


How Do You Get BioMats?
BioMats are rare biological materials scattered throughout the ship—found in chests, dropped by enemies, and hidden in high-risk areas. They’re highly valuable and absolutely essential for unlocking BioBoost upgrades.

In the lore, they’re fragments of genetic material drawn from the same source that caused the Orpheus’s infection. What exactly that means… well, that’s for you to uncover.

But one thing is certain: with every upgrade, you feel just a little less human.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/88de1c6375e286309135f68a2b2ebed2ca01c753.jpg"]

With Version 1.0 only seven weeks away, it’s time for a closer look at the core gameplay systems that power your survival and progression aboard the Orpheus. Let’s break down your main objectives, combat tools, and the resources you’ll rely on run after run.


GOALS
The ship is infected and the systems are breaking down. You're the last line of defense.

Your mission: travel deep into the ship to reactivate critical systems and stop the infection before it consumes everything. With ODY-6 lighting your way, explore quarantined sectors, eliminate hostile threats, and lift lockdowns to proceed. Once you find the ship's internal transport bays, you choose your path forward and continue. Be sure to check which path you take, as some may lead to valuable resources or drop you into even deadlier encounters.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/aa4a4c32b0cd54c4a50cd09feabc48693047fbc3.png"]
WEAPONS AND AUGMENTS
In Moros Protocol, you’ll carry one melee weapon and two ranged weapons at a time. Weapons fall into three categories: melee, energy, and physical. Melee uses stamina. Ranged weapons rely on either energy or physical ammo, depending on the type.

Each weapon has its own level and rarity. You can upgrade levels at vendors you find along your journey, but rarity is locked in. That makes high-rarity drops especially valuable—they hit harder and often come with unique traits.

Augments are where you shape your playstyle. Some are simple stat boosts like extra health or movement speed. Others change the way you fight, like giving you a double jump or modifying how your weapon behaves in combat.

We’ve also added Implanted Augments. These are stronger than regular augments, but they come with a cost. They might increase your damage but reduce your defense, or give you speed while draining stamina faster. Once implanted, they can’t be removed for the rest of the run.

Pick your tools, build your loadout, and adapt to survive.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/a142a768179d4b0595c0def2ec2dbf2441779018.png"]


RESOURCES
You’ll gather five core resources as you fight and explore, each helping you progress, unlock content or improve your build.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/4a346d13c18276e91033585e7575730eca9c4d3c.png"]

Resource List:

BioMats – Used to upgrade your BioBoost

Energy Ammo – Powers blue energy weapons

Physical Ammo – Powers orange physical weapons

Door Keys – Opens locked sectors, vendor rooms, and loot chests

Utopia Credits – Used to buy weapons, upgrades, and augments

Break crates, loot chests, and defeat enemies to collect more. Or... just hope you survive long enough to use them.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/0e741c52403d53dbc93550b5a418e21be0de1d4e.png"]
BIOBOOST
Death is not failure. Death is data.

If you fall in battle, you’ll restart from the beginning of the current act. But don’t worry, your BioMats carry over, allowing you to permanently enhance your core abilities between runs.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/cb43eb523a05f8f6fc05477d307454e67a9315ed.png"]

We’ll be covering the full BioBoost system in detail next Thursday, so stay tuned!

notes.content:
Know your enemy! That's a core tenet of being an Orphean. Whether you're fighting Freorra Corpos or alien threats, you must understand them. And what better way than to use their own weapons against them.

Weapons & Augments #4
We've loved all the support you've given us thoroughout our recent playtests, however, there's still plenty of weapons & augments you haven't seen! Let's talk about some of them today.

WEAPONS
Absolver ⚔️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/cd6094ae70b3643abf64b39a2184af8233bcbf0b.png
A mechanical chainsaw blade designes specifically for cutting tough flesh and bones. Standard Catharis anti-darkphage weapon.

Burning Heat🔫
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/1617816c96f78086bc387b4d1525c45970f4df88.png
Originally created by a cook with a passion for burning things, this makeshift flamethrower is now a classic DIY recipe found in space web, which you can quickly make with things you find in a spaceship kitchen.

AUGMENTS
Bloody Aid ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/e19a4ab1c4f098fa79bbf804bafad747204ab460.png
The monsters of the Darkphage are snappy and vicious. The likelyhood of getting slashed, bitten and shot are very high. However, this isn't all negative. If you pick up an augment like Bloody Aid, you turn 25% of damage received is fills your healing shot meter every time you get hit.

Stay Healthy ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/3eb574c1094743ee856155b1e36d1316e680051a.png
Healthy Melee & Healthy Weapons are upgrades for the masters of doding. If you believe you can keep your health at full, then these augments are for you. When at full HP, increase Melee weapon damage by 60% or increase Ranged weapon damage by 50% respectively.

notes.title: Dev Diary #10 - Weapons and Augments #3 + Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
Acthana X weaponry - built to last lightyears. Take a piece of Terra into the void. Whatever's out there, Acthana X has your back.

Weapons & Augments #3
The Orpheus is crawling with unknown threats. But it’s not all doom and gloom — today’s dev diary is about fighting back electrical weapons and tactical augments. Let’s dive in. 🩸

The Conduit ⚔️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/46206aa5a329ee09e6594ac6db3a0aa6edd0775a.png
Rumored to be forged by a mad engineer deep in the Orpheus, this blade was originally meant for fire rescue. Now? It's perfect for slicing through flesh and synthetic matter alike. It's brutal, swift, and has a thirst for pain.

Dual Str8Fires 💥 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/b3589a348f73b323fcf3e722efc0c21ac617c89a.png
Repurposed from old Earth tech as the evolution of "Uzi", these dual-wielded SMGs define the phrase "spray and pray." With large mags doubling as recoil dampeners, they’re chaotic, fast, and dangerously fun in tight corridors.

XM LED Strobe ⚡
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/153f91e34595b26a582cd114a139b715052fd54a.png
Once a mining laser, now a handheld cannon. The XM LED Strobe was turned into a weapon of rebellion during the Gravel-3 uprising. It’s raw, unstable, and powerful; no safety switch, just fire.

Enhance your gear. Enhance yourself. Here are two augments that can shift the tide mid-run.

Powerslash ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/24f5abd46e274872b8f8515083a54749db967f12.png
Supercharge your melee. After a fully charged swing, dodge to activate a 1-second 200% damage boost. Perfect for carving through Darkphage before they can blink.

Impact Wave ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/912c74c737278454746a0c6ff2b0927b4b60caab.png
Land hard, hit harder. Slamming into the ground now releases a shockwave... but be careful, your jumps will cost more stamina. High risk, high impact.

notes.title: Moros Protocol Playtest #4 - Now Live!
notes.content:
Soldiers stick together. That's a core tenet Orpheans believe in fervently. Facing the universe alone is a curse.

Good day, Orpheans!

Our 4th playtest is now live! This playtest brings a big change... Co-op is now available.
Grab a friend and face the darkness... together.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/0879a3da5d07d7c18d59f3fc3d15f771ac440450.gif

How to join the playtest
Head over to the Moros Protocol Steam page and hit the "Request Access" button on the playtest.
The Playtest app should now be available in your Steam library. This process might take a minute, so refresh if it doesn't pop up immediately.

Patch Notes
New Weapons 💥  
 The Conduit (Melee)
One of a series of bladed weapons rumoured to have been crafted by a mad engineer deep in the ship’s bowels with a penchant for pain and a sprinkle of surprise. Though its creation was bound for fire-fighting, a downward swing is bound to cut most non-metal materials easily.
 The Dual Str8Fires (Physical)
Repurposed from forgotten Earth tech, Str8Fires are lightweight submachine guns that are perfect for dual-hand showdowns. These weapons are the definition of "spray and pray", as their large magazines also act as recoil compensators and prevent unwanted muzzle rise 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/46206aa5a329ee09e6594ac6db3a0aa6edd0775a.png 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/b3589a348f73b323fcf3e722efc0c21ac617c89a.png
New Content 
 Online Co-op is now available in the main menu.
 Enabled more Bioboost upgrades.
 Added Challenge Rooms.
 Two new enemy types - Darkster Larvae & Variant Zombie 
Changes & Bug Fixes 
 Kick now destroys cocoons and Secret Room doors.
 During the loading screen (travel screen), the screen now fades to full black.
 Spitclaw weapon has new visual effects; its projectile now deals area-of-effect damage.
 Fixed area-of-effect damage on enemies.
 Ranged weapon fire rate now remains consistent during weapon swapping.
 Fixed enemies spawning on top of boxes and interactables.
 Damage numbers now shrink after reaching a certain size to avoid obstructing the player's view.
 Dodge behaviour changed: melee attacks no longer track, but ranged attacks still do.
 Adjusted spawn areas for enemies.
 Slot animations are now faster.
 Corruption mechanics have been adjusted.
 Chest opening trigger is now more forgiving.
 Items and pickups are now disabled during cutscenes.
 Duplicate resolutions are now hidden in the settings menu when the OS reports the same resolution multiple times (per refresh rate). FPS remains a separate setting. 
Known Issues
With the release of Co-op, we know there are some issues that may arise. Here are some problems you might face and how to work around them. Always feel free to message us in our Discord server or in the Steam forums if you have any issues! 
 Co-op  - Desync may be possible in subsequent co-op sessions.,
Workaround: After each co-op session, it is advised to close/relaunch the title to start another co-op session afresh.
 Screen Resolution - Changing resolutions may cause display issues
Workaround (to default): Delete the PixelReign folder in Registry Editor. To find this:
- Search and open up Registry Editor
- Open HKEY_CURRENT_USER folder
- Open Software folder
- Locate the PixelReign folder.
- Delete the PixelReign folder.

Have fun! This is our most exciting playtest so far. See you in the stars 💫

notes.title: Dev Diary #8 - What the Darkphage Leaves Behind
notes.content:
It has seeded the infinite void with denizens of hatred. It waits in silence, until the pride of mankind demands correction. Unfettered, it brings lasting equality through annihilation. It is destruction incarnate. It is the Darkphage.

Echoes in the Dark
Something unnatural has taken hold aboard the Orpheus. Its crew changed, Its corridors stalked by things that shouldn’t exist. Today, we're revealing some of the threats you'll encounter in Moros Protocol.

Larvae
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/c151367a30c02160145b92380fd66d3b558753f1.png

These creatures scuttle through the Orpheus with an unsettling purpose; seeking out the living. Small and fragile at first, they’re easy to dispatch... but don’t get comfortable. The longer they persist, the more they change. And the more dangerous they become.

Twisted Orpheans
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/f143cb39a5bf797523032e532ee2a69eb729fb3c.png

Once-human figures now roam the halls, grotesquely altered. They move with brute force but sluggish steps, as if dragged by something within. Their glowing chests may hint at a weakness, but facing them means confronting what your crewmates have become.

Nychoraptors
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/50ec194179fab53b1da500140eaaa4f782014ee0.png

These creatures no longer resemble anything from the Orpheus. Fast, vicious, and disturbingly agile, they are the stuff of nightmares. Watch for the glint of an eye where one should never be... targeting it may be your only chance.

Thank you for reading, and get ready for our playtest this weekend. You might want to grab a friend as co-op kicks off tomorrow! See you in the stars 💫

notes.title: Dev Diary #6 - Weapons and Augments #2
notes.content:
Know your enemy! That's a core tenet of being an Orphean. Whether you're fighting Freorra Corpos or alien threats, you must understand them. And what better way than to use their own weapons against them.

Good day, Orpheans!

There's even more weapons and augments to talk about in today's developer diary! We're going to focus on using the enemy against itself and picking up some corrupted weaponry.

WEAPONS
The Orpheus is crawling with unknown enemies. But it's not all doom and gloom! Use their own bodies against them with these weapons 🩸

Bonesaw ⚔️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/52d976cf7ff008e8ea4b4189ec9218b5f9dc6167.png
A sharp jawbone from a Darkphage with remarkable toughness. Its convenient shape makes it an effective close-combat weapon.

Spitclaw 🔫
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/e5b026de50840484cb328f731816e2abb7599f85.png
An energy-generating gland from a Darkphage, it can manipulate magnetic fields to create and propel balls of plasma. It seems to be able to sustain itself if given enough food. Recently seen in our playtest—did you get a chance to play with it?

Bonespitter 🔫
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/0f8eb5adfa202361699108949fe61c59503c6650.png
This grotesque mass of organs is capable of propelling bone-like projectiles at devastating speeds, inflating its lung and releasing the gas with immense pressure.

AUGMENTS
Last time we talked about augments that improved your health and stamina. Now, we're going to look at some augments that actively give you new abilities throughout your run.

Dodge Defence ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/4310bf02f7a262fdc9278aa2346f183305fabf69.png
Your dodge is a powerful tool. When a Darkphage infectant is swinging its failing arms toward your torso, you need to get out of the way. However, there's more to your dodge with these augments. Like Aftershock, which drops a mini time bomb when you dodge, and Static Discharge, which leaves an electric field in your wake. However, be careful, as these extra abilities are going to increase your dodge stamina cost.

Keep it Moving ⬆️
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/02d9d042c305b3ef6ed2497b25add979c901f3c9.png
Increase your player speed with augments like Kinetic Boosters and Scout Boots. This will make it much harder for the Darkphage to take you down. Then combine these abilities with Run n Gun to increase weapon damage by up to 160% while moving. Become a speed machine and a blur of bullets!

You will be able to find some of these weapons and more in the upcoming playtest this weekend (starting tomorrow, the 9th of May). Be sure to sign up once it goes live at 4 PM BST. See you in the stars 💫

notes.title: Dev Diary #5 - The Orpheus
notes.content:
Assistance Request - The Orpheus
We’ve called in one of Acantha X’s Capital-class battleships to break the stalemate. Freorra’s forces are numerous, their attacks relentless, our lines won’t hold much longer. The Orpheus should have left Hyperspace by now. It’s carrying much-needed reinforcements, along with enough munitions and supplies to turn the tide... without them, we’ve lost. Where is that damn ship?

Inside the Orpheus
Moros Protocol takes place aboard the Orpheus, Acantha X’s colossal deep-space warship. Today, we’re peeling back the hull plating and giving you a look at its history, purpose, and what it means for the war effort.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/857baef77843fc29191c3fd6bc182e58ee84141c.png
The Orpheus is a Capital Battleship; a mobile fortress-city designed to carry millions of cryo-slept troops across the stars. It’s outfitted with cutting-edge weaponry, training grounds, agriculture domes, and a fleet of escort ships. In short, it’s a symbol of Acantha X’s military dominance.

Now, with the war against Freorra Industries locked in a brutal deadlock, both sides are growing desperate. Rumors swirl that Acantha X is preparing to deploy a classified weapon to force an end to the conflict. But with tensions escalating and every second counting, all eyes are on the Orpheus.

Will it arrive in time to tip the scales?
And just how far is Acantha X willing to go in the name of victory?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/5972bc275e611e929875ff59fdf88d0940434e31.png
Thanks for reading, and we can’t wait for you to explore the Orpheus during our upcoming playtests.

See you in the stars,✨
— Pixel Reign 🚀

notes.title: Dev Diary #3 - Meet Alex
notes.content:
You have to have faith that he will protect you. Because when the chips are down, he's the only bet I'd make.

Good day, Orpheans!

In Moros Protocol, you play as the last remaining soldier aboard the deep-space vessel, the Orpheus. His name is Alex, and he might just be the universe’s last hope.

Alex wakes up from cryo-sleep. System guides him through the now-abandoned spaceship. As he explores, he discovers a robot called ODY-6. It doesn’t take long before he realizes something is wrong. There’s an infection on the ship that he needs to survive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/608eca7972d3fc91c7fdd244355913c884f27e27.png

Alex is one of many Orpheans who were meant to protect the ship. Except something within the cryopod went wrong. After waking up, his memories and skills seem to have completely disappeared. Now, he goes against a mysterious alien infection known only as the Darkphage.

The monsters spawning from the jagged maw of death were too powerful. What's worse is that when we sent our solider to die, they came back infected. We only have one more option... we only have him.

The day has come, Orpheans!

Below is a list of the weapons and augments that you can find in this playtest build. We look forward to hearing your feedback, be sure to join our discord to get direct access to the Devs!

WEAPONS 💥 
 W.E.L.L Gauntlet (Energy)
A hand-equipped weapon that launches discs in an accelerating rate. XOR Weapon-Enhanced Level of Lethality Gauntlet houses 3 motors to build centrifugal force and launch rate based on the discharge hold time.
 GX7 Short Barrel Blaster (Energy)
Hephaestus Weapons Tech's range of special ordinance firearms that include armor piercing rounds that, in the words of their marketing department, "both sizzle and pop."
 Nano Ravid (Energy)
A sleek rifle designed for the upper echelons of command, it blends high tech nano-polymer ordnance with elegance in looks. Fueled by a high-pressure plasma canister, it allows 20 shots per reload.
 MKII (Energy)
Painfully Weaponized Nanotech Devices are haptically enhanced weapons that can be utilized on the field of battle to remove the need for manual reloads. The state-of-the-art reload technology will infuse the air around it and charge protons while spinning its barrel.
 Charging Thunder (Melee)
A standard crew vibro-blade replete with a nano-sharpened edge that can charge to increment its damage output.
 Sarcophage (Melee)
A Darkphage tumor growing on a piece of metal that heals the user upon eliminating an enemy. Sometimes you can see it's eye looking around, seemingly interested in flesh.
 Gada Devi (Melee)
Standard issue heavy mace created by XOR and used by heavy infantry. Designed to inflict maximum damage to heavy armored targets.
 Master Enforcer (Physical)
Developed as standard issue for crews expecting to require above average firepower, this reliable handgun comes with nano-enhanced ordnance to avoid weapon jamming and lower recoil.
 Golden Sunset (Physical)	
Gold plated in places to appeal to those with both the credits to spend and the eloquence to kill in style, the Golden Sunset Series aims to impress your victim for the few moments of life they have left.
 TVA-5 (Physical)
The Tactical Variable Action Shotgun is a 6-slug, cock-per-round, robust shotgun that will never let you down. While possessing of certain redundancies in branding, is an all-round weapon easily found at black markets throughout the quadrant.
 R55 Long-Scope (Physical)
A sniper's favorite, R55 is a long and sleek heavy ordnance rifle developed by HWT. It's heavy damage is countered by its heavy recoil and bullet-cocking time.

 Shrapnel Shot: Each shot has a chance to fire shrapnel projectiles.

 Speed Amp: Inscreases weapon attack speed/fire rate by 15%.
 Aftershock: Drop a mini time bomb when dodging. Dodge costs more stamina.

notes.title: Dev Diary #1 - Who are we?
notes.content:
The hardest thing about Deep Space? Sometimes you hear a creak or a snap in a random part of the ship, and the only person you have to blame is an engineer a million miles away. That and the constant barrage of alien lifeforms trying to rip you apart.

Good day, Orpheans!

Thank you for all your support throughout our recent update. We're so excited to finally bring Moros Protocol in 2025. There's so much to talk about while we build to the final version of the game... so, we plan to do weekly dev diaries every single Thursday! This means you'll get insights into development and leave suggestions to help us shape Moros Protocol into the deep space boomer shooter of your dreams.

Today, we're going to talk about the team behind the game, Pixel Reign.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/d18d263cc98f2aa33b19b72e8d984e7e2e10af3f.png

The studio was founded in 2018, however, Nick Larin the founder has been working on games since 1999. Nick worked as developer for "Darkfall 2: The Unholy Wars".  He then worked on many mobile games (most of them not online anymore). Pixel Reign started with the creation of a game named Robbie Swifthand. They collaborated with a Greek mobile studio to make Neonverse. After that, tons of mobile games again as B2B (dark times) while slowly starting the Darkverse project.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/32893031fc3cf37c96df8a7262df6a5cadee1b68.png

Darkverse was a personal project Nick worked on 2009-2011, A 2.5d spaceship game which was never finished.  You can watch some footage from the original game here!

[previewyoutube=ea53YFrJsek;full][/previewyoutube]

But the story and world were fleshed out, so the team decided to create a game in the same universe as a prologue to that game. That's how Darkverse: Rogue came to be, which is now Moros Protocol. 

Moros Protocol started as a side project back in 2019, while the team were working on external projects to help sustain the studio. Around September 2022 we were able to focus more on the project and we slowly were fleshing out the version you saw last year. Now, with the help of Super Rare Originals, the team has grown!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42294246/345a68125a67c0909bd729d8ba198afdbe10961f.png

When asked what he was most excited for players to jump into, Nick said this
"Personally I just love when people get to experience a world I created or worked on, and see how they approach everything in their own way. This is something you can only do in videogames, where you see others literally "live" through an experience you created."

We're so excited for Moros Protocol to release later this year! We look forward to seeing you next week for another Dev Diary!

Upcoming Playtests
We announced last week that we plan to have consistent playtests on the road to launch. Those will kick off very soon right here on Steam. We'll release a full schedule into our discord very soon (will update Steam later). Be sure to join our discord to get the latest updates on Steam Playtests and an easy place to leave feedback for the devs and find fellow Orpheans to get hype.

Thanks for reading! See you in the stars

notes.title: 🎮🎄 A Holiday Update & A New Name 🎄🎮
notes.content:
Hello, Darkverse: Rogue fans!

As we head into the holiday season, we have some exciting news to share. After much thought and reflection, we’ve decided to rename our game. This new name ties deeply into the game’s lore and our creative vision.

Moros, in Greek mythology, is the personification of impending doom and fate—a force that no one can escape. It’s a concept that perfectly reflects the tension and stakes at the heart of our game. This change also honours our Greek heritage of our team and the mythological inspiration that’s been a guiding light for the project.

The new name of the game shall be...
Moros Protocol

While this year has been a quieter one for updates, rest assured that Moros Protocol has been evolving into something truly special. We’ve been working tirelessly behind the scenes to refine the game and bring our vision to life.

Mark your calendars, because 2025 is going to be an incredible year for us—and for you, our players. A big announcement is on the horizon, and we can’t wait to share what’s next.

From everyone on the team, we wish you a Merry Christmas and a wonderful holiday season. Thank you for your continued support, and we can’t wait to embark on this new chapter together!

Stay safe,
The Pixel Reign Team
